issue.title: Native bob query --tasks takes ~7 s and ~1.58 GB RSS for any filter on the live vault

task_type_fields.impact:
`bob query --tasks` is documented as the shell/scripting surface for Tasks
queries (docs/dataview.md). At about 7 s and 1.5 GB per call it is unusable
for interactive or per-metric use: any dashboard, stats, or smoke-test caller
that runs several queries pays tens of seconds and gigabytes. On busy agent
hosts it also risks memory pressure. The daily-stats research had to recommend
a dedicated single-pass scanner instead of building on `bob query --tasks`.
task_type_fields.location: src/native/dataview/tasks/mod.rs (run / CLI bob query --tasks path) and src/native/dataview index build
task_type_fields.repro:
Found by research.0u.cld while researching a daily-stats feature (report
`research:202610/daily_stats_tracking__cld.md`, artifact
`file:explicit:59ece264447c32b8330667cd`, §3.4) on apollo (16 cores, idle), with
the live `~/bob` vault (6,234 `.md` files, 13.5 MB of Markdown, ~3,500 `#task`
lines) and the installed `~/.cargo/bin/bob` built from master `ab9fbaf`.

Every native `bob query --tasks` run costs about 6.3-7.1 s wall time and about
1.58 GB peak RSS, even for a trivial filter with no `by function` (so this is
NOT the bob-cli-33 sandbox: `maybe_sandbox` is lazy now and the vault Tasks
`globalQuery` is only `path does not include _conflicts`):

    /usr/bin/time -f "%e s %M KB" bob query --format paths --tasks 'done on 2026-10-10' >/dev/null
    # 6.27 s 1581216 KB
    /usr/bin/time -f "%e s %M KB" bob query --format paths --tasks '' >/dev/null
    # 6.74 s 1586732 KB
    /usr/bin/time -f "%e s %M KB" bob query --format json --tasks $'done after 2025-10-01\nnot done' >/dev/null
    # 6.54-6.94 s, ~1580000 KB (3 runs)

For comparison, on the same vault and host:
- `bob freshness list -f json` (native Tasks rich-task path): 1.62 s, 34.7 MB RSS
- `bob plan`: 0.68 s; `bob ready`: 1.68 s
- a single-pass Python scan of every `.md` file computing per-day task and Pomodoro counts: 0.47 s

`strace -f -e trace=openat` shows the query opening 12,467 `.md` paths, so
each note is opened about twice. That alone doesn't explain a ~117x
memory amplification over the Markdown size. The root cause is not yet
identified (candidates: the full Dataview vault index/link resolution built for
`query.file.*`, per-task cloning in the CLI `run` path, or output assembly).

issue.creation_reason: While measuring vault-scan costs for the daily-stats design, a trivial native `bob query --tasks` filter took ~7 s and ~1.58 GB RSS on a 13.5 MB vault, while `bob freshness list` scans the same vault in 1.6 s and 35 MB; that gap points at a defect in the CLI Tasks query path, not inherent cost.

payload.description: Earlier Tasks-query cost bug (eager JS sandbox); its lazy-sandbox fix is in place, so this cost has a different root cause in the same module
